import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# O-minimal structures with a trans-exponential function

Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?

A structure $(M, <, \dots)$ on a linear order is *o-minimal* if every subset of $M$ definable
with parameters is a finite union of points and open intervals. A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to
\mathbb{R}$ is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates every finite iterate
$\exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ of the exponential function. Since "trans-exponential" only makes
sense relative to the real exponential function, the question is understood, as is standard, for
expansions of the real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$: is there an o-minimal expansion
of the real ordered field in which some trans-exponential function is definable?

A complete theory is o-minimal if and only if it is the theory of an o-minimal structure
(Knight, Pillay, Steinhorn), so the question is stated here for structures on $\mathbb{R}$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, O-minimal theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/o-minimal)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [L. van den Dries, C. Miller, *Geometric categories and o-minimal structures*, Duke Math. J. 84 (1996)](https://doi.org/10.1215/S0012-7094-96-08416-1)
-/

universe u v

namespace OMinimal

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Filter

/-- A subset $s$ of a linear order $M$ is a finite union of points and open intervals, where the
endpoints of the intervals are taken in $M \cup \{-\infty, +\infty\}$. -/
def IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals {M : Type*} [LinearOrder M] (s : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (P : Finset M) (I : Finset (WithBot M × WithTop M)),
    s = ↑P ∪ ⋃ p ∈ I, {x : M | p.1 < (x : WithBot M) ∧ (x : WithTop M) < p.2}

/-- A first-order `L`-structure on a linear order $M$ is *o-minimal* if the ordering $<$ is
definable and every subset of $M$ that is definable with parameters from $M$ is a finite union of
points and open intervals. -/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language) (M : Type*) [LinearOrder M] [L.Structure M] : Prop :=
  (Set.univ : Set M).Definable₂ L {p : M × M | p.1 < p.2} ∧
    ∀ s : Set M, (Set.univ : Set M).Definable₁ L s → IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals s

/-- A first-order `L`-structure on $\mathbb{R}$ is an *expansion of the real ordered field*
$(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$ if the ordering, addition and multiplication are definable in it. -/
def IsExpansionOfRealOrderedField (L : FirstOrder.Language) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 < p.2} ∧
    (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable L {x : Fin 3 → ℝ | x 0 + x 1 = x 2} ∧
    (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable L {x : Fin 3 → ℝ | x 0 * x 1 = x 2}

/-- A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is *trans-exponential* if for every $n$,
$f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$, where $\exp^{(n)}$ is the $n$-fold
iterate of the exponential function. -/
def IsTransExponential (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x

/-- The exponential function itself is not trans-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 26]
theorem not_isTransExponential_exp : ¬ IsTransExponential Real.exp := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (h 2).exists
  simp only [Function.iterate_succ, Function.iterate_zero, Function.comp_apply, id_eq] at hx
  have : x < Real.exp x := by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp x]
  exact absurd (Real.exp_lt_exp.mpr this) (not_lt.mpr hx.le)

/-- An open interval $(a, \infty)$ is a finite union of points and open intervals. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals_Ioi {M : Type*} [LinearOrder M] (a : M) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals (Set.Ioi a) := by
  refine ⟨∅, {((a : WithBot M), (⊤ : WithTop M))}, ?_⟩
  ext x
  simp

/-- A finite set is a finite union of points and open intervals. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals_finset {M : Type*} [LinearOrder M] (P : Finset M) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals (P : Set M) :=
  ⟨P, ∅, by simp⟩

/--
Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?

Precisely: is there a first-order structure on $\mathbb{R}$ which expands the real ordered field
$(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$, is o-minimal, and in which some function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is definable (with parameters) such that, for every $n$,
$f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 26]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : L.Structure ℝ),
      IsExpansionOfRealOrderedField L ∧ IsOMinimal L ℝ ∧
        ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | f p.1 = p.2} ∧
          IsTransExponential f := by
  sorry

end OMinimal

modeling_decisions: 'O-minimal first order theory' is formalized as an o-minimal first-order *structure* on ℝ. A complete theory is o-minimal iff it is the theory of an o-minimal structure (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), and 'trans-exponential' only makes sense relative to the real exponential, so the standard reading (van den Dries–Miller: 'is there an o-minimal expansion of the real field defining a transexponential function?') is used, as the decomposition notes prescribe.

'Expansion of the real ordered field (ℝ, <, +, ·)' is formalized as: the ordering, the graph of addition and the graph of multiplication are definable (with parameters) in the structure, rather than requiring the language to literally contain these symbols via `LHom.IsExpansionOn`. Interdefinable structures have the same definable sets, so o-minimality and definability of f are unaffected and the existence question is equivalent; this avoids heavy `Language.ring`/`Language.order` instance plumbing inside an existential.

The structure is required to expand (ℝ, <, +, ·), not (ℝ, <, +, ·, exp). By Miller's growth dichotomy, exp is definable in any o-minimal expansion of the real field that defines a non-polynomially-bounded function, so the two readings are equivalent; the decomposition table's reading was followed.

Definability is always with parameters from all of ℝ (`(Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable ...`), matching the usual convention in o-minimality ('definable' = definable with parameters); naming constants preserves o-minimality so this does not change the existence question.

The trans-exponential function is taken to be a total function f : ℝ → ℝ with definable graph, with the growth condition `∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x` (strict inequality, for all sufficiently large x, for every n including n = 0, which is implied by n = 1). A definable function on some (a, ∞) can be extended by 0 to a total definable function, so totality is no loss.

O-minimality is defined as: `<` is definable and every definable (with parameters) subset of M is a finite union of points and open intervals, where interval endpoints range over `WithBot M × WithTop M` (i.e. M ∪ {−∞, +∞}); closed/half-open intervals are covered as open interval ∪ endpoints. The bespoke `IsOMinimal` takes any `LinearOrder M`; the DLO requirement of the general definition holds automatically for ℝ, the only instance used.

The language is universe-polymorphic (`FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}`), so the theorem has universe parameters u v. Any structure on ℝ is interdefinable with one whose symbol types live in `Type`, so the truth value of the right-hand side is independent of u, v; a universe-polymorphic statement is at least as general as fixing `Language.{0,0}`.

Three `@[category test]` lemmas with short proofs are included to validate the bespoke definitions (exp is not trans-exponential; `Set.Ioi a` and finite sets are finite unions of points and intervals), following CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# O-minimal structures with a trans-exponential function

A structure $(M, <, \dots)$ on a linearly ordered set is *o-minimal* if every subset of $M$
definable with parameters from $M$ is a finite union of points and open intervals (with
endpoints in $M \cup \{\pm\infty\}$). Wilkie's theorem says that the real ordered field with
the exponential function, $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot, \exp)$, is o-minimal. Every function
definable in this structure, and in every other known o-minimal expansion of the real field,
is eventually bounded by some finite iterate $\exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ of the exponential.

The following question is open: does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a
trans-exponential (rapid growth) function? Following the literature, this is read as: is there
an o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$ in which some
*trans-exponential* function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is definable, that is, a function
$f$ such that, for every $n$, $f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$.

Since the complete theory of an o-minimal structure is an o-minimal theory, asking for an
o-minimal *structure* on $\mathbb{R}$ is equivalent to asking for an o-minimal *theory* with a
model of this form. Structures are considered up to interdefinability, as is customary in
o-minimality: an expansion of the real field is a structure on $\mathbb{R}$ in which $<$, $+$
and $\cdot$ are definable. Since `ℝ : Type`, every structure on `ℝ` is interdefinable with one
whose language lives in `Language.{0, 0}`, so it is no loss of generality to quantify over
such languages only.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, O-minimal theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/o-minimal)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [A. J. Wilkie, *Model completeness results for expansions of the ordered field of real
  numbers by restricted Pfaffian functions and the exponential function*, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9
  (1996)](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-96-00216-0)
- [L. van den Dries, *Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures*, Cambridge University Press
  (1998)](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511525919)
-/

namespace OMinimal

open Set Filter

section LinearOrder

variable {M : Type*} [LinearOrder M]

/-- A subset of a linear order `M` is an *open interval* if it is of the form `(a, b)`, `(a, ∞)`,
`(-∞, b)` or `(-∞, ∞)` for some `a b : M`, i.e. an open interval with endpoints in
`M ∪ {-∞, +∞}`. -/
def IsOpenInterval (J : Set M) : Prop :=
  (∃ a b, J = Ioo a b) ∨ (∃ a, J = Ioi a) ∨ (∃ b, J = Iio b) ∨ J = univ

/-- A subset `X` of a linear order `M` is a *finite union of points and open intervals* if
there are a finite set `X₀ ⊆ M` and finitely many open intervals `I₁, …, Iᵣ` (with endpoints in
`M ∪ {-∞, +∞}`) such that `X = X₀ ∪ I₁ ∪ … ∪ Iᵣ`. -/
def IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals (X : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X₀ : Set M) (𝓘 : Set (Set M)), X₀.Finite ∧ 𝓘.Finite ∧ (∀ J ∈ 𝓘, IsOpenInterval J) ∧
    X = X₀ ∪ ⋃₀ 𝓘

/-- A point is a finite union of points and open intervals. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals_singleton (a : M) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals {a} :=
  ⟨{a}, ∅, finite_singleton a, finite_empty, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- An open interval `(a, b)` is a finite union of points and open intervals. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals_Ioo (a b : M) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals (Ioo a b) :=
  ⟨∅, {Ioo a b}, finite_empty, finite_singleton _, by simp [IsOpenInterval], by simp⟩

/-- A closed interval `[a, b]` with `a ≤ b` is a finite union of points and open intervals. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals_Icc {a b : M} (h : a ≤ b) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals (Icc a b) := by
  refine ⟨{a, b}, {Ioo a b}, toFinite _, finite_singleton _, by simp [IsOpenInterval], ?_⟩
  ext x
  simp only [mem_Icc, mem_union, mem_insert_iff, mem_singleton_iff, sUnion_singleton, mem_Ioo]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
    rcases h₁.eq_or_lt with rfl | h₁
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inl rfl)
    rcases h₂.eq_or_lt with rfl | h₂
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inr rfl)
    exact Or.inr ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
  · rintro ((rfl | rfl) | ⟨h₁, h₂⟩)
    · exact ⟨le_rfl, h⟩
    · exact ⟨h, le_rfl⟩
    · exact ⟨h₁.le, h₂.le⟩

end LinearOrder

/-- An `L`-structure on a linearly ordered type `M` is *o-minimal* if the order `<` is definable
and every subset of `M` that is definable (with parameters from `M`) is a finite union of points
and open intervals. -/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language) (M : Type*) [LinearOrder M] [L.Structure M] : Prop :=
  (∅ : Set M).Definable₂ L {p : M × M | p.1 < p.2} ∧
    ∀ X : Set M, (univ : Set M).Definable₁ L X → IsFiniteUnionOfPointsAndIntervals X

/-- An `L`-structure on `ℝ` is an *expansion of the real ordered field* `(ℝ, <, +, ·)` if the
order relation and the graphs of addition and multiplication are definable without parameters. -/
def IsExpansionOfRealField (L : FirstOrder.Language) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 < p.2} ∧
    (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable L {v : Fin 3 → ℝ | v 0 + v 1 = v 2} ∧
    (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable L {v : Fin 3 → ℝ | v 0 * v 1 = v 2}

/-- A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates every finite iterate
of the exponential function: for every `n`, `exp^[n] x < f x` for all sufficiently large `x`. -/
def IsTransexponential (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x

/-- No finite iterate of the exponential function is trans-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 26]
theorem not_isTransexponential_exp_iterate (k : ℕ) : ¬ IsTransexponential Real.exp^[k] :=
  fun h => by simpa using (h k).exists

/-- A trans-exponential function tends to `+∞`. -/
@[category API, AMS 26]
theorem IsTransexponential.tendsto_atTop {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : IsTransexponential f) :
    Tendsto f atTop atTop :=
  tendsto_atTop_mono' atTop ((hf 0).mono fun _ hx => hx.le) tendsto_id

/-- Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function? That is, is there an o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field $(ℝ, <, +, ·)$ in
which some trans-exponential function $f : ℝ → ℝ$ is definable, i.e. some definable $f$ with
$f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $x$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 26]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{0, 0}) (_ : L.Structure ℝ),
      IsOMinimal L ℝ ∧ IsExpansionOfRealField L ∧
      ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L f.graph ∧ IsTransexponential f := by
  sorry

end OMinimal

modeling_decisions: 'O-minimal first order theory' is formalized as an o-minimal *structure* on ℝ (a language L with an L.Structure ℝ instance). This is equivalent to the theory reading because the complete theory of an o-minimal structure is an o-minimal theory (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), and an o-minimal theory with a trans-exponential function must have a model of the form (ℝ, <, +, ·, …) for 'trans-exponential' to make sense; noted in the module docstring.

Following the decomposition notes and the literature (van den Dries, Miller, Wilkie), the structure is required to be an expansion of the real ordered field (ℝ, <, +, ·). 'Expansion' is taken up to interdefinability: `IsExpansionOfRealField L` requires the order relation and the graphs of + and · to be ∅-definable (rather than literally symbols of L). This is the customary convention in o-minimality and yields an equivalent existence statement, while avoiding Mathlib's heavier `LHom.IsExpansionOn`/`CompatibleRing`/`OrderedStructure` plumbing.

O-minimality (`IsOMinimal L M`) is defined for an arbitrary `LinearOrder M`: `<` is ∅-definable and every subset of `M` definable with parameters from all of `M` (`(univ : Set M).Definable₁ L X`) is a finite union of a finite set and finitely many open intervals `(a,b)`, `(a,∞)`, `(-∞,b)`, `(-∞,∞)` with endpoints in `M`. The dense-without-endpoints hypothesis in Wikipedia's definition is not built into the general definition since it holds automatically for ℝ, the only case used. The `<`-definability clause is repeated in `IsExpansionOfRealField` (redundant but keeps each definition self-contained).

Trans-exponential: `IsTransexponential f := ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x`, i.e. f eventually strictly dominates every finite iterate of exp (including n = 0, i.e. the identity). This matches the standard definition (Miller / van den Dries); strict vs. non-strict inequality is immaterial here since exp^[n+1] > exp^[n] eventually.

The trans-exponential function is required to be total (`f : ℝ → ℝ`) and definable *with parameters* (`(univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L f.graph`), the standard meaning of 'definable' in o-minimality. Functions definable only on a neighbourhood of +∞ extend definably by 0, so this is no restriction.

The language is fixed to `FirstOrder.Language.{0, 0}` to avoid a universe-polymorphic theorem. Since `ℝ : Type`, any structure on ℝ is interdefinable with one whose relation symbols are indexed by `Set (Fin n → ℝ) : Type`, so this loses no generality; this is explained in the module docstring.

namespace OMinimal

open FirstOrder

/--
A first-order structure on the reals is o-minimal if every subset of `ℝ` definable with
parameters is a finite union of intervals and points. Here intervals and points are uniformly
represented by order-connected sets.
-/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Set ℝ, (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₁ L s →
    ∃ pieces : Set (Set ℝ), pieces.Finite ∧
      (∀ t ∈ pieces, Set.OrdConnected t) ∧ s = ⋃₀ pieces

/-- The language obtained by adding arbitrary symbols to the languages of rings and orders. -/
abbrev RealExpansionLanguage (L : FirstOrder.Language) :=
  FirstOrder.Language.ring.sum (FirstOrder.Language.order.sum L)

/--
The structure on `RealExpansionLanguage L` which interprets the ring and order symbols as the
standard operations and order on `ℝ`, and the remaining symbols according to `struc`.
-/
noncomputable def realExpansionStructure (L : FirstOrder.Language) (struc : L.Structure ℝ) :
    (RealExpansionLanguage L).Structure ℝ := by
  letI : L.Structure ℝ := struc
  letI : FirstOrder.Language.ring.Structure ℝ :=
    (FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ).toStructure
  letI : FirstOrder.Language.order.Structure ℝ :=
    FirstOrder.Language.orderStructure ℝ
  infer_instance

/--
Does there exist an o-minimal first-order expansion of the real ordered field in which a
trans-exponential function is definable? More precisely, does such an expansion define a function
`f : ℝ → ℝ` which, for every `n : ℕ`, is eventually strictly larger than the `n`-fold iterate of
the real exponential function?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language) (struc : L.Structure ℝ),
      letI := realExpansionStructure L struc
      IsOMinimal (RealExpansionLanguage L) ∧
        ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
          (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ (RealExpansionLanguage L) f.graph ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in Filter.atTop, (Real.exp^[n]) x < f x := by
  sorry

end OMinimal
modeling_decisions: Following the decomposition table's standard reading, the existential object is an o-minimal first-order expansion of the standard real ordered field, rather than an arbitrary ordered model. Its complete theory supplies the corresponding o-minimal theory mentioned in the list entry.

The expansion language is the sum of Mathlib's ring language, order language, and an existentially quantified extra language. The associated structure interprets the ring and order symbols by the standard operations and order on ℝ.

O-minimality is stated directly: every unary subset definable with arbitrary real parameters is a finite union of order-connected subsets. Over ℝ these are intervals (including singleton intervals), so this is the finite-union-of-intervals-and-points condition from the background article.
A function is definable when its graph is definable with arbitrary real parameters in the expansion.

Trans-exponential growth means that for every natural n, the function eventually strictly dominates the n-fold iterate of the standard real exponential. Including n = 0 adds the identity iterate, which is redundant given domination of the positive iterates.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# O-minimal theories with a trans-exponential function

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks: *does there exist an o-minimal first order theory
with a trans-exponential (rapid growth) function?*

A structure $(M, <, \dots)$ on a linearly ordered set is *o-minimal* if every subset of $M$
definable with parameters is a finite union of points and open intervals (with endpoints in
$M \cup \{\pm\infty\}$). A theory is o-minimal if all of its models are; the complete theory of
an o-minimal structure is o-minimal (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), so the question is equivalently
a question about o-minimal structures.

Since "trans-exponential" only makes sense relative to the exponential function, the question is
understood, as in the literature (van den Dries, Miller, Wilkie), for o-minimal expansions of the
real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$: is there such an expansion that defines a function
$f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that eventually dominates every finite compositional iterate
$\exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ of the exponential function? Equivalently: is there an o-minimal
expansion of the real field that is not exponentially bounded? No known o-minimal expansion of
the real field (e.g. $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{an}, \exp}$, Pfaffian closures)
defines a trans-exponential function.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, O-minimal theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/o-minimal)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* L. van den Dries, *Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures*, London Mathematical Society
  Lecture Note Series 248, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
* C. Miller, *Tameness in expansions of the real field*, Logic Colloquium '01,
  Lecture Notes in Logic 20, ASL, 2005, 281–316.
-/

namespace OMinimal

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- A subset of a linearly ordered set is a *point or open interval* if it is a singleton or an
open interval with endpoints in `M ∪ {-∞, +∞}`, i.e. it is one of `{a}`, `Set.Ioo a b`,
`Set.Ioi a`, `Set.Iio a` or `Set.univ`. -/
def IsPointOrOpenInterval {M : Type*} [LinearOrder M] (s : Set M) : Prop :=
  (∃ a, s = {a}) ∨ (∃ a b, s = Set.Ioo a b) ∨ (∃ a, s = Set.Ioi a) ∨ (∃ a, s = Set.Iio a) ∨
    s = Set.univ

/-- An `L`-structure on a linearly ordered set `M` is *o-minimal* if the order `<` is definable
(without parameters) and every subset of `M` that is definable with parameters from `M` is a
finite union of points and open intervals (with endpoints in `M ∪ {-∞, +∞}`). -/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language) (M : Type*) [LinearOrder M] [L.Structure M] : Prop :=
  (∅ : Set M).Definable₂ L {p : M × M | p.1 < p.2} ∧
    ∀ s : Set M, (Set.univ : Set M).Definable₁ L s →
      ∃ F : Finset (Set M), (∀ I ∈ F, IsPointOrOpenInterval I) ∧ s = ⋃₀ ↑F

/-- An `L`-structure on `ℝ` is an *expansion of the real field* if the graphs of addition and
multiplication are definable without parameters. (The order `<` is then also definable, since
`x < y ↔ ∃ z, z ≠ 0 ∧ y = x + z * z`.) -/
def IsExpansionOfRealField (L : FirstOrder.Language) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable L {v : Fin 3 → ℝ | v 0 + v 1 = v 2} ∧
    (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable L {v : Fin 3 → ℝ | v 0 * v 1 = v 2}

/-- A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates every finite
compositional iterate `exp ∘ ⋯ ∘ exp` of the exponential function: for every `n`,
`exp^[n] x < f x` for all sufficiently large `x`. -/
def IsTransexponential (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in Filter.atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x

/--
Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?

Formalized as: is there an o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field
$(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$ in which some function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that
eventually dominates every finite iterate $\exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ of the exponential
function is definable (with parameters)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{0, 0}) (_ : L.Structure ℝ),
      IsExpansionOfRealField L ∧ IsOMinimal L ℝ ∧
        ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | f p.1 = p.2} ∧
          IsTransexponential f := by
  sorry

/-- The exponential function itself is not trans-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isTransexponential_exp : ¬ IsTransexponential Real.exp := by
  intro h
  simpa using (h 1).exists

/-- The real field, as a structure for the language of rings, is an expansion of the real
field. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isExpansionOfRealField_ring :
    letI := Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ
    IsExpansionOfRealField Language.ring := by
  letI := Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Set.empty_definable_iff]
    refine ⟨Term.equal (Term.var 0 + Term.var 1) (Term.var 2), ?_⟩
    ext v
    simp
  · rw [Set.empty_definable_iff]
    refine ⟨Term.equal (Term.var 0 * Term.var 1) (Term.var 2), ?_⟩
    ext v
    simp

/-- The real field is o-minimal: its definable sets are the semialgebraic sets
(Tarski–Seidenberg). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 14]
theorem isOMinimal_ring_real :
    letI := Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ
    IsOMinimal Language.ring ℝ := by
  sorry

end OMinimal

The single-slot decomposition and its suggested standard reading (o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field defining a function eventually dominating every finite iterate of exp; '(rapid growth)' as a gloss; existential Prop with answer(sorry)) are correct and were followed.
modeling_decisions: 'o-minimal first order theory' is formalized via an o-minimal *structure* on ℝ. This is the standard reading in the literature (van den Dries, Miller, Wilkie) and is equivalent: the complete theory of an o-minimal structure is o-minimal (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), and conversely every model of an o-minimal theory is o-minimal.

Since 'trans-exponential' only makes sense relative to exp, the structure is required to be an expansion of the real ordered field (ℝ, <, +, ·). Without this the question would be trivial (e.g. (ℝ, <, h) for a fixed-point-free increasing homeomorphism h is o-minimal, and h may be chosen with arbitrarily fast growth). By Miller's growth dichotomy any o-minimal expansion of the real field defining a trans-exponential function also defines exp, so the 'expansion of (ℝ, <, +, ·, exp)' reading coincides with this one.

'Expansion of the real field' is formalized set-theoretically (as in van den Dries's 'Tame Topology'): the graphs of + and · on ℝ are definable without parameters (`IsExpansionOfRealField`), rather than by requiring the ring/order symbols to literally belong to the language via a language map. This is equivalent up to interdefinability, which does not affect o-minimality or the class of definable functions. The order < is not separately required here since it is definable from + and · over ℝ; `IsOMinimal` separately requires < to be ∅-definable (Wikipedia's set-theoretic axiom '< ∈ S₂').

`IsOMinimal L M` for a `LinearOrder M`: < is ∅-definable and every subset of M definable *with parameters* (`(Set.univ : Set M).Definable₁ L s`) is a finite union of sets of the form {a}, Ioo a b, Ioi a, Iio a, univ (open intervals with endpoints in M ∪ {±∞}, and points), matching Wikipedia's definition. Density of the order is not built into the definition (it is a precondition on M in Wikipedia's definition, automatically true for ℝ). Used only with M = ℝ.

`IsTransexponential f` := ∀ n, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, exp^[n] x < f x (f eventually strictly dominates every finite compositional iterate of exp). Strict vs non-strict is immaterial under the ∀ n. The alternative reading 'f is not eventually bounded by any iterate of exp' is equivalent for functions definable in an o-minimal expansion of the real field (definable functions are eventually comparable, and exp is definable by Miller's dichotomy once f is not polynomially bounded).

f is taken to be a total function ℝ → ℝ definable with parameters. WLOG: a definable function on a neighbourhood of +∞ can be extended by 0; parameters can be named as constants without affecting o-minimality.

The language is fixed at universe level `FirstOrder.Language.{0, 0}` so that the theorem has no universe parameters. This loses nothing: any structure on ℝ (in any universe) has the same definable sets as a Type-0 language with one relation symbol per definable subset of ℝⁿ.

/-- A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of points and open intervals: there are a
finite set $X_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and finitely many open intervals $I_1, \dots, I_r$ with

def IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints (X : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X₀ : Finset ℝ) (I : Finset (EReal × EReal)),
    X = ↑X₀ ∪ ⋃ ab ∈ I, {x : ℝ | ab.1 < x ∧ x < ab.2}

/-- A first-order structure on the real line (in a language `L`) is *o-minimal* if every subset
of $\mathbb{R}$ that is definable with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of points and
open intervals. -/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  ∀ X : Set ℝ, (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₁ L X → IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints X

with the relation symbol `≤`) in the ordered field of real numbers. -/

every finite iterate of the exponential function: for every $n$, $f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all

  (∅ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 < p.2} ∧

exponential and a trans-exponential function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$? Here
trans-exponential means that, for every $n$, $f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all sufficiently large
